sourcing_note_en: Every question here is grounded in item targets read from the files on disk rather than from memory. Modules 9, 10 and 11 are verifiable and carry nine questions each. Module 8 is not: its level files are not on disk, and the only assertions about it that survive anywhere are its level 52 to 53 verb block — बताना, पूछना, मिलना, लाना — and the fact that its brief made collocation a game in its own right. It therefore carries three questions rather than the seven or eight an even split would give it, and every one of those three tests something independently attested. When module08.json is merged, four more questions should be added and the weighting corrected.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these three verbs takes ने in the perfective?
questions.explanation_en: वह बोला, मैं लाया, वह भूला — all without ने. उसने कहा takes it, which is why the pair is taught side by side.

questions.prompt_en: मैंने लड़की ___ बुलाया — what fills the gap?
questions.explanation_en: को is obligatory with a person as object, and it switches the verb to neutral agreement.

questions.prompt_en: मैंने उसको देखा. Why is देखा not देखी, even if उस refers to a woman?
options: को on the object blocks agreement, so the verb goes neutral
questions.explanation_en: This is the proof that को is doing grammatical work rather than just marking a person.

questions.prompt_en: हमने फ़िल्म ___ है — which form?
questions.explanation_en: फ़िल्म is feminine and takes no को, so the verb agrees with it. ने does not change that in the present perfect.

questions.prompt_en: उन्होंने किताबें पढ़ी थीं. What is the verb agreeing with?
questions.explanation_en: Feminine plural object with no को, so पढ़ी थीं. The ने subject never controls agreement.

questions.prompt_en: वह भूला and उसने याद किया. Why does one take ने and not the other?
options: भूलना is one of the three verbs that refuse ने; करना does not
questions.explanation_en: The exception sits in the verb itself, not in the sentence around it.

questions.prompt_en: राम ने सीता को देखा. Which noun does the verb agree with?
questions.explanation_en: ने blocks the subject and को blocks the object, so nothing is left to agree with.

questions.prompt_en: ने is best understood as what?
options: An ordinary postposition, which puts the noun before it into the oblique
questions.explanation_en: Which is why लोग becomes लोगों before it, exactly as before any other postposition.

questions.prompt_en: मैं पानी लाया. Why no ने?
options: लाना is one of the three verbs that refuse it
questions.explanation_en: बोलना, लाना and भूलना are the three, and they have to be learned as a set.

questions.prompt_en: मुझे भूख लगी है means what?
options: I am hungry, with मैं as subject
Hunger has struck me — the hunger is the subject
questions.explanation_en: The person is a destination rather than an actor, which is the organising idea of the whole module.

questions.prompt_en: Which verb goes with दर्द and बुखार?
questions.explanation_en: भूख, प्यास and ठंड take लगना; दर्द and बुखार take होना. The choice is fixed per sensation.

questions.prompt_en: Which verb goes with नींद and ग़ुस्सा?
questions.explanation_en: नींद आना and ग़ुस्सा आना — they arrive. डर, in the same level, takes लगना instead.

questions.prompt_en: उन्हें आम पसंद ___ — which form?
questions.explanation_en: पसंद agrees with the thing liked, not with the person. आम is plural here, so हैं.

questions.prompt_en: मुझे यह जगह अच्छी लगी. Why अच्छी?
options: अच्छा agrees with जगह, which is feminine — and so does लगना
questions.explanation_en: Two words move together, which is what distinguishes अच्छा लगना from पसंद है.

questions.prompt_en: मुझे हिंदी आती है means what?
questions.explanation_en: आना for skills and languages. जानना is used for facts and people rather than abilities.

questions.prompt_en: मुझे जाना चाहिए means what?
questions.explanation_en: चाहिए with an infinitive is should. With a noun — मुझे पानी चाहिए — it is need.

questions.prompt_en: दो घंटे लगते हैं. Which sense of लगना is this?
questions.explanation_en: One of the five senses the module catalogues — felt, seemed, attached, taken, and struck.

questions.prompt_en: When the experiencer is a noun rather than a pronoun, what happens?
options: It stays in the direct case
It takes को and goes oblique — बच्चे को, लोगों को
questions.explanation_en: मुझे and उसे are simply the fused forms of the same को.

questions.prompt_en: In a compound verb, which part carries the tense and agreement?
questions.explanation_en: The main verb sits in its bare stem and the vector does all the grammatical work.

questions.prompt_en: Which vector turns the action inward, toward the doer?
questions.explanation_en: खा लेना, समझ लेना, कर लेना. देना turns it outward.

questions.prompt_en: उसने खाना खा ___ — which vector makes it decisive and outward-facing?
questions.explanation_en: Eating is inward, so लेना. देना would be wrong here — you do not eat for somebody else's benefit.

questions.prompt_en: Which compound refuses ने?
questions.explanation_en: The जाना vector makes the whole compound intransitive, however transitive the main verb was.

questions.prompt_en: रो पड़ना means what?
options: To burst into tears — sudden and involuntary
questions.explanation_en: पड़ना marks something that happens to you rather than something you do.

questions.prompt_en: What separates सकना from पाना?
options: सकना is ability; पाना is managing to, often against difficulty
questions.explanation_en: नहीं कर सका says you were unable; नहीं कर पाया says you did not manage it.

questions.prompt_en: Put the obligation ladder in order from weakest to strongest.
questions.explanation_en: चाहिए is should, है is have to, पड़ा is had no choice.

questions.prompt_en: पीना becomes पिलाना in the causative. What has happened to the vowel?
options: It has shortened, and a ल has appeared
questions.explanation_en: पीना, पिलाना, पिलवाना — and खाना, खिलाना, खिलवाना does the same thing.

questions.prompt_en: मैंने उससे काम करवाया. What is से doing?
options: Naming the person who actually did the work
questions.explanation_en: The second causative names an agent, and से is how it is named.

questions.prompt_en: Why does Module 8 make collocation a game in its own right?
options: Because knowing a word and picking the wrong verb with it is what makes a learner sound translated
Because it is easier to test
questions.explanation_en: The same principle governs पासवर्ड डालना and मुद्दा उठाना in Module 13.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these Module 8 verbs takes को on the person and a second object?
questions.explanation_en: उसने मुझे बताया कि — बताना takes को, while कहना and पूछना take से. Module 13 level 19 returns to exactly this.

questions.prompt_en: मिलना has two quite different uses. Which pair is right?
options: To meet somebody, and for something to be available or received
questions.explanation_en: उनसे मिला, I met them; मुझे मिल गया, I got it. Both recur throughout Modules 10 to 13.

open_flags: Module 8 carries three of thirty questions rather than the seven or eight an even split would give it, because its level files are not on disk and only its level 52-53 verb block and its collocation principle are independently attested. Four further questions should be added once module08.json is merged.

Module 9's own checkpoints 1 and 2 and its mock remain blocked for the same reason — module09_levels01-05.json and module09_levels06-10.json are not on disk, so levels 1 to 10 of that module cannot be assessed. The nine questions here draw only on levels 11 to 16, which are present.
